name: Colosseum
description: Rome’s great amphitheatre still stands in the heart of the ancient city. Walk the outer rings and arches to feel how crowds once poured in for public games.

name: Trevi Fountain
description: The Trevi Fountain fills a tight square in central Rome with cascading water and baroque sculpture. Tradition says toss a coin over your shoulder if you hope to return.

name: Pantheon
description: A Roman temple later consecrated as a church, the Pantheon is famous for its concrete dome and open oculus. Inside, a calm circular hall is lit by a single shaft of daylight from above.

name: Milan Cathedral
description: Milan’s Gothic cathedral fills Piazza del Duomo with marble spires and a wide facade. Climb toward the terraces for close views of the statues and the city beyond.

name: Florence Cathedral
description: Santa Maria del Fiore anchors Florence’s historic centre with Brunelleschi’s great dome. The patterned marble facade and baptistery sit around Piazza del Duomo.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
description: The freestanding bell tower of Pisa’s cathedral leans across the green Campo dei Miracoli. Walk the lawn for the classic view of tower, duomo, and baptistery together.

name: Castel Sant'Angelo
description: Hadrian’s mausoleum later became a fortress and papal refuge on the Tiber. From the ramparts you look along the bridge of angels toward St Peter’s.

name: Pompeii
description: The buried Roman city of Pompeii opens as a vast archaeological park at the foot of Vesuvius. Streets, houses, and the forum still show daily life frozen by the eruption.

name: Pizza al taglio
description: Stampd treats pizza as a Naples city food stamp — not a named restaurant. This photo shows classic Margherita-style pizza as a stand-in for the street-food culture the stamp celebrates.

name: Gelato
description: Stampd treats gelato as a Rome city food stamp — not a specific gelateria. The photo is a representative Italian artisanal gelato display for that food-culture stamp.

name: Mercato Centrale
description: Florence’s central market hall gathers produce stalls downstairs and a busy food court above. Come for Tuscan ingredients, sandwiches, and a sit-down bite under the iron roof.

name: Spanish Steps
description: A broad Baroque stair climbs from Piazza di Spagna toward the Trinità dei Monti church. Sit on a lower step to watch the square, then walk up for the view over the rooftops.

name: Villa Borghese
description: Villa Borghese is Rome’s great central park of lawns, tree avenues, and museum villas. Rent a bike or stroll to the lake temple for a quieter hour away from the densest streets.

name: Ponte Vecchio
description: Florence’s medieval bridge still carries shops across the Arno in a tight row of windows. Cross at dusk when the river reflects the goldsmith shutters and the corridor above.

name: Piazza Navona
description: An elongated square follows the shape of Domitian’s stadium, lined with cafés and fountains. Bernini’s Fountain of the Four Rivers anchors the middle of the open space.

name: Rialto Bridge
description: The stone arch of the Rialto is the oldest of the Grand Canal’s four bridges. Climb the steps for the classic view of water traffic and the market side of San Polo.

name: Positano
description: Positano spills down the Amalfi cliffs in stacked pastel houses above a small beach. Walk the steep lanes for sea views and the harbour square at the bottom.

name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
description: Milan’s 19th-century glass-roofed arcade links Piazza del Duomo to Piazza della Scala. Look up at the iron-and-glass vault and the mosaic floor under the central octagon.

name: Venice Carnival
description: Venice Carnival fills the city with costumes and masks before Lent, with many public moments in and around Piazza San Marco. It is seasonal and date-limited each year — check the official calendar before you go.

name: Palio di Siena
description: Twice each summer, Siena’s contrade race bareback around Piazza del Campo in the Palio. The square is packed for trial runs and the race days in July and August — a short, seasonal tradition, not a year-round show.

name: Mercato di Testaccio
description: A neighbourhood market hall in Testaccio with produce stalls and casual lunch counters.

name: Porta Palazzo Market
description: One of Europe’s large open-air markets spreads around Piazza della Repubblica in Turin.
